rule.en:
A question in English puts a helping verb before the subject. For most verbs this is **do**, **does** (he, she, it) or **did** (the past), and the main verb goes back to its base form: **Do you come here every evening?** **Does Meg bark?** **Did you see the fox?** (not *Does Meg barks?*, not *Did you saw?*).

The negative works the same way: **don't**, **doesn't**, **didn't** + the base form: **I don't know.** **Meg doesn't bark.** **We didn't go.**

No do with **be**, **can**, **will** or **must**: they just swap places with the subject: **Are you cold?** **Is it far?** **Can you swim?** Their negatives: **isn't**, **can't**, **won't**.

A question word comes first: **Where do you live?** **What does it mean?** But when who or what is the subject, there is no do: **Who lives here?** **What happened?**

Short answers repeat the helping verb: **Yes, I do.** / **No, she doesn't.** / **Yes, I can.**
rule.sl:
V slovenščini je vprašanje lahko enako kot trditev, le z drugačnim glasom (**Prideš?**) ali z **ali** / **a**. Angleščina pa postavi pred osebek pomožni glagol. Pri večini glagolov je to **do**, **does** (he, she, it) ali **did** (preteklik), glavni glagol pa je v osnovni obliki: **Do you come here every evening?** (Prihajaš sem vsak večer?) **Does Meg bark?** **Did you see the fox?** (ne *Does Meg barks?*, ne *Did you saw?*).

Zanikanje gre enako: **don't**, **doesn't**, **didn't** + osnovna oblika: **I don't know.** (Ne vem.) **Meg doesn't bark.** **We didn't go.**

Brez do so **be**, **can**, **will** in **must**: le zamenjajo mesto z osebkom: **Are you cold?** (Te zebe?) **Is it far?** **Can you swim?** Zanikanje: **isn't**, **can't**, **won't**.

Vprašalnica je na začetku: **Where do you live?** (Kje živiš?) **What does it mean?** Kadar je who ali what osebek, do ni: **Who lives here?** **What happened?**

Kratki odgovori ponovijo pomožni glagol: **Yes, I do.** / **No, she doesn't.** / **Yes, I can.**
rule.it:
In italiano la domanda può essere uguale all'affermazione, cambia solo il tono (**Vieni?**). L'inglese invece mette un verbo ausiliare prima del soggetto. Per la maggior parte dei verbi è **do**, **does** (he, she, it) o **did** (passato), e il verbo principale torna alla forma base: **Do you come here every evening?** (Vieni qui ogni sera?) **Does Meg bark?** **Did you see the fox?** (non *Does Meg barks?*, non *Did you saw?*).

La negazione funziona allo stesso modo: **don't**, **doesn't**, **didn't** + forma base: **I don't know.** (Non lo so.) **Meg doesn't bark.** **We didn't go.**

Niente do con **be**, **can**, **will** e **must**: si scambiano di posto con il soggetto: **Are you cold?** (Hai freddo?) **Is it far?** **Can you swim?** Negazione: **isn't**, **can't**, **won't**.

La parola interrogativa va per prima: **Where do you live?** (Dove abiti?) **What does it mean?** Se who o what è il soggetto, niente do: **Who lives here?** **What happened?**

Le risposte brevi ripetono l'ausiliare: **Yes, I do.** / **No, she doesn't.** / **Yes, I can.**
rule.de:
Im Deutschen stellt man für die Frage einfach das Verb nach vorn: **Kommst du?** Im Englischen geht das nur mit wenigen Verben. Bei den meisten steht **do**, **does** (he, she, it) oder **did** (Vergangenheit) vor dem Subjekt, und das Hauptverb steht in der Grundform: **Do you come here every evening?** (Kommst du jeden Abend hierher?) **Does Meg bark?** **Did you see the fox?** (nicht *Come you here?*, nicht *Does Meg barks?*).

Die Verneinung geht genauso: **don't**, **doesn't**, **didn't** + Grundform: **I don't know.** (Ich weiß es nicht.) **Meg doesn't bark.** **We didn't go.**

Kein do bei **be**, **can**, **will** und **must**: Sie tauschen wie im Deutschen den Platz mit dem Subjekt: **Are you cold?** (Ist dir kalt?) **Is it far?** **Can you swim?** Verneinung: **isn't**, **can't**, **won't**.

Das Fragewort steht vorn: **Where do you live?** (Wo wohnst du?) **What does it mean?** Ist who oder what das Subjekt, dann ohne do: **Who lives here?** **What happened?**

Kurze Antworten wiederholen das Hilfsverb: **Yes, I do.** / **No, she doesn't.** / **Yes, I can.**

examples.en: Do you come here every evening?

note.en: do + you + come (not Come you here?).
note.sl: do + you + come (ne Come you here?).
note.it: do + you + come (non Come you here?).
note.de: do + you + come (nicht Come you here?).

examples.en: Does Meg bark at the ponies? — No, she doesn't.
examples.sl: Ali Meg laja na ponije? — Ne, ne laja.
examples.de: Bellt Meg die Ponys an? — Nein.

note.en: does + bark: the -s is already in does.
note.sl: does + bark: -s je že v does.
note.it: does + bark: la -s è già in does.
note.de: does + bark: das -s steckt schon in does.

examples.en: Where do you live? — I live in Keswick.
examples.de: Wo wohnst du? — Ich wohne in Keswick.

examples.en: I don't know the way to the tarn.
examples.sl: Ne poznam poti do gorskega jezerca.
examples.it: Non conosco la strada per il laghetto.
examples.de: Ich kenne den Weg zum Bergsee nicht.

note.en: be takes no do: Are you …? (not Do you are …?).
note.sl: be ne dobi do: Are you …? (ne Do you are …?).
note.it: be non vuole do: Are you …? (non Do you are …?).
note.de: be ohne do: Are you …? (nicht Do you are …?).

examples.en: Can you swim, Poppy? — Yes, I can.
Who lives in the old mill? — Mr Tyson does.
examples.sl: Kdo živi v starem mlinu? — Gospod Tyson.
examples.it: Chi abita nel vecchio mulino? — Il signor Tyson.
examples.de: Wer wohnt in der alten Mühle? — Herr Tyson.

note.en: who is the subject: no do.
note.it: who è il soggetto: niente do.
note.de: who ist das Subjekt: ohne do.
